name: amount-pad

frames.best_why: Amount $125 entered with the button full green and reading Sent $125.

tagline: Tap a keypad to set an amount, then send it in one press.
summary: A send-money keypad. Digits spring into a large amount that shrinks to fit, with quick presets, a balance line and a cap that refuses amounts past the limit.
appearance: A tall dark rounded card. A small orange initials badge and a Send to Maya Chen @maya line sit at the top over a huge amount, a balance line and three preset pills. Below, a three-by-four keypad of digits, a dot and a backspace sits over a full-width Send button.
behaviour: Tapping a key springs the digit into the amount while the number shrinks to stay on one line and commas slot in. Send wakes once a value exists, turns green with a tick after sending, then clears; typing past the cap shakes the number and shows a limit message.
demo_content: Sending to Maya Chen @maya, balance $3,204.18, presets $20, $50 and $100.
search_phrases: keypad to enter a payment amount
enter an amount with big digits
use_when: A payment step wants a big, thumb-friendly keypad instead of a text field, with quick preset amounts.
avoid_when: It is built for one-off transfers under a fixed cap; editing a saved amount or entering long figures is cramped.
customise: Recipient, currency, cap, balance, presets and an onSend callback are props; colours, key order and animation springs are fixed in the source.
weight_why: About a dozen buttons and a few spring animations; nothing runs when idle.

a11y.note: Keyboard entry works and the amount is announced; Send is only aria-disabled, so it stays focusable and clickable while empty.

issues: Send is only aria-disabled, so it looks inert but still takes clicks when empty.
polish_why: Large self-fitting amount, clear keypad rhythm and a satisfying send-to-green state.
